721 AM EDT Tue Aug 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 137 AM EDT Tuesday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 137 AM EDT Tuesday...

1. Tranquil weather is expected today and Wednesday as high 
pressure builds over the region. 

2. Seasonably warm and unsettled weather returns for the end of 
the week, with chances for showers and thunderstorms. 

3. Classic northern trough-southern ridge summer weather 
pattern will bring above normal temperatures and multiple small 
scale weather systems for the weekend into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 137 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A pleasant day is expected across the region today as 
high pressure continues to nose into the region, bringing a period 
of drier weather. Some valley fog that has developed overnight will 
gradually dissipate through the morning, with mostly clear skies and 
sun expected for this afternoon. High temperatures today will climb 
into the upper 70s to mid 80s. Another day of tranquil conditions is 
expected for Wednesday as the region remains under the influence of 
ridging, with high temperatures a few degrees warmer under light 
southerly flow with daytime highs climbing into the 80s areawide. 
Overall, it looks like a few pleasant summer days are on tap for the 
region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Heading into the latter half of the week, warm and 
unsettled weather is expected as the region remains sandwiched 
between high pressure to the south and an upper level trough to the 
north, with zonal flow bringing several different disturbances to 
the region. With broad southwesterly flow ushering in plenty of 
moisture, chances for showers and thunderstorms will be possible. 
Latest guidance shows decent instability across the region Thursday 
afternoon, which combined with ample moisture and decent forcing may 
lead to thunderstorm development in the afternoon, with the 
potential for some stronger thunderstorms possible if all the 
ingredients align, although details will become clearer as we get 
closer. Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are also 
expected for Friday. In addition to the shower chances increase 
later this week, the increased moisture will allow for dewpoints to 
climb into the upper 60s to near 70 at times, making it feel 
increasingly muggy and uncomfortable later this week. High 
temperatures will climb into the 80s, with heat indices climbing 
into the upper 80s and near 90.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Over the weekend, an upper low will mature on the 
western edge of the Hudson Bay while a large western upper high 
flattens out and settles east. This will produce a channeled flow 
pattern that commonly sends small scale features racing east in a 
speedy jet stream. This usually also means that the forecast 
predictability will be low, as coarse resolution models may not 
always accurately depict these smaller, convectively-influenced 
systems within the fast flow pattern.

Assessing different ensemble suites, most indicate largely above 
normal PWATs, although there is a signal for a brief pocket of dry 
air. Some have that dry air in place on Sunday, some have it on 
Monday, and a minority have it on Saturday. So Saturday appears the 
most likely to feature scattered (even numerous) showers and 
thunderstorms over the weekend. Between Saturday and next Tuesday, 
there's at least a trough per day passing east, and so there could 
be some rain for each day. Towards the middle of next week, the 
large scale pattern doesn't change too much, but the northern trough-
southern ridge pair shifts east. This will place us a bit more under 
the influence of the upper low. So after a period of above normal 
temperatures, we will start trending back towards normal. The 
question will be how amplified that upper low remains. Still showers 
can't be completely discounted given the upper low nearby.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 12Z Wednesday...Fog is in the process of lifting this
morning. Skies will trend clear. For the most part, winds will
be west to northwest at 5 to 9 knots, though we should warm 
enough that KPBG observes a lake breeze this afternoon, though 
with some uncertainty on timing. A few gusts 15 to 18 knots are
likely at KMPV, KEFK, and KMSS. After 22-00z, winds will trend
light or terrain driven. Some thin high clouds could approach
from the south, but did add 2SM from 08z to the end of this TAF
cycle for KSLK and KMPV.

TSRA.
Friday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Saturday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
